messages.subject: [GRASS-stats] Anyone still using GRASS 5?
messages.body_plain:
On Wed, 29 Sep 2010, Roger Bivand wrote:

> Is anyone still using GRASS 5 and the R "GRASS" package? With GRASS 6.*, the 
> spgrass6 package is actively maintained. If nobody is using GRASS 5, I would 
> like to archive and retire the R "GRASS" package. However, if someone is 
> actively using GRASS5 and the matching R "GRASS" package, I'll keep it active 
> until you let me know that you are through.

As no response has been forthcoming, the R GRASS package for interfacing 
GRASS 5 has been retired from active CRAN distribution, but will remain 
available as a source package at:

http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/GRASS/

Roger

Then I installed the packages

Then from the shell:

R

Then load these libraries

library(spdep)
library(maptools)
library(boot)
library(Matrix)
library(lattice)

I read the raster

index_water_2009<-readRAST6("index_water_2009")

At this point I stopped. I saw on the mailing list and some tutorials.

I can not understand the syntax to use.

It only works on vector?

Someone can give me some help?

Thanks

>
> Hy everyone.

> sensing (with decimals).
>
> I would like to calculate the Moran's index and the index of Getis and Ord

> Then I installed the packages
>

> install.packages("maptools",dependencies=TRUE)
>

> R
>
> Then load these libraries

> library(spgrass6)
> library(spdep)
> library(maptools)
> library(boot)
> library(Matrix)

>
> I read the raster
>
> index_water_2009<-readRAST6("index_water_2009")
>
> At this point I stopped. I saw on the mailing list and some tutorials.
>
> I can not understand the syntax to use.

Well, in rasters the number of "observations" is typically very large, 
probably artificially so, depending on the "natural" resolution of the 
phenomena of interest. Consequently, in rasters one almost always finds 
strong positive spatial autocorrelation, because the cells do not 
represent well the actual entities. If you need to do this, you can try 
in Spearfish:

library(spgrass6)
gmeta6()
execGRASS("g.region", parameters=list(res="150"))
# to coarsen the input resolution
gmeta6()
elev <- readRAST6("elevation.dem")
GT <- slot(elev, "grid")
library(spdep)
nb_rook <- dnearneigh(coordinates(elev), 0, mean(slot(GT,
   "cellsize"))*1.05)
summary(elev)
# note NAs, need to subset to handle:
mt <- moran.test(elev$elevation.dem, nb2listw(nb_rook), na.action=na.omit)
# using spatial weights row standardisation
mt

Hope this helps,

Roger
